items.title: Bill Bourgeois Interview, 1959-12-10
items.q: and he begged me to come to work with him at Knicks.

ctx.x: Okay, let's see. I think you'd better get a little closer to the mic. We were talking about Dan LeBlanc going over to his house.

Yeah, with his afternoon sessions, drink beer, and a whole crowd of saxophone players, just to see how it sounds. And well it went on like that. The fellas different jobs working around. And then in 1936 I went to New York, just on my own, and just decided to go and see what it was. And I worked around different clubs in New York, you know. And then Sharky came up there right after. I was working on a job in Brooklyn, and he begged me to come to work with him at Knicks. And incidentally we had this Henry Adler…
Had you planned to make records with Sharky?

items.title: Sharkey Bonano Interview, 1966-11-09
items.q: And so I got a band together, George Brunus. George Brunus. First time I heard George in person. Bill Bourgeois, a fella by the name of Turk on the bass, and Bowman.

ctx.x: In other words, it was a cobweb place. Yeah, I heard you there. Down in the cellar. And so I got a band together, George Brunus. George Brunus. First time I heard George in person. Bill Bourgeois, a fella by the name of Turk on the bass, and Bowman. I don't know if you know Bowman, Red Bowman, he played piano.
Yeah, yeah, the pianist. He was from New York, I guess.
